title: Hyderabad Student Killed as Lighting Truss Collapses During College Dandiya Fest
excerpt: Sony Narayana Das, an EEE student at MVSR Engineering College in Nadergul, died when a lighting stand fell during the Sangamam-2026 Dandiya programme; at least 12 others were injured and the chief minister ordered strict action.
body:
• One student, Sony Narayana Das from the Electrical and Electronics Engineering branch, was killed when a lighting truss collapsed during a Dandiya programme at MVSR Engineering College in Nadergul, Hyderabad.
  • Police said 12 others were injured; PTI-based reporting put the injured at 14 and said they were out of danger — the college said about nine were admitted and CT scans cleared them.
  • The collapse happened minutes before the Dandiya programme was to end on Saturday evening, during strong winds at the Sangamam-2026 fest, according to the college director.
  • Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy expressed shock, ordered the injured be given the best treatment, and directed officials to identify those responsible and take strict action.

An engineering student was killed and at least 12 others were injured when a lighting truss collapsed during a Dandiya celebration at MVSR Engineering College in Nadergul, on the outskirts of Hyderabad, on Saturday evening. The incident occurred under Adibatla police station limits in Rangareddy district, according to ANI reporting. Police said the injured were shifted to hospital for treatment.

Daily Jagran, citing PTI, reported 14 injured and said they were out of danger, and that the student was rushed to a private hospital but died during treatment. The differing injured counts — 12 in the police statement carried by ANI, 14 in PTI reporting — reflect early counts from the campus and hospitals and may be revised as officials confirm admissions.

Ten minutes before the programme ended

The Dandiya programme was part of Sangamam-2026, the college's two-day national-level technical and cultural festival held on October 16 and 17. College Director Prasanna Kumar said the Dandiya was arranged at students' request from 5:30 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. to conclude the cultural day, and that a strong gale struck about ten minutes before it was to conclude.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2111676117170229448

"Unfortunately, we lost one young student, Sony Narayana Das from the EEE branch. About nine students were admitted to the hospital. We acted immediately, using our own college vehicles, as waiting for the 108 ambulance was taking time."

— Prasanna Kumar, Director, MVSR Engineering College

Kumar described the collapse as an unforeseen natural mishap caused by sudden, severe gales and said students taken for CT scans had been declared out of danger. Eyewitness accounts carried by ANI said the metal truss supporting decorative stage lights fell onto a group of female students dancing on the ground.

Family and political reaction

Suresh, an uncle of the victim, alleged basic safety precautions were not taken and demanded answers, telling reporters the family first thought the injury was minor. BJP leader Andela Sriramulu Yadav, who visited the campus, alleged the poles were unstable and erected without adequate support and called for arrests if negligence is established. Those claims are allegations at this stage; police have said they are investigating whether mandatory permissions and safety certifications were obtained by the college management and event contractors.

What happens next

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy expressed shock, conveyed condolences to the bereaved family, directed officials to ensure the best possible treatment for the injured, and instructed them to identify those responsible and take strict action, according to the Chief Minister's Office. A large police deployment was sent to the campus as tensions rose among students and parents. The investigation will need to establish the structure's design and anchoring, the wind conditions at the time, and who certified the temporary lighting rig for a crowd event.
